node-1.label: One-day-old male infant has not passed stool since birth and has increased bilious vomiting and abdominal swelling

node-2.label: Born at term, birth weight 3.1 kg, no significant prenatal history, uncomplicated delivery

node-3.label: Since birth, no stool passage, increased bilious vomiting, abdominal swelling; anus in normal position with well-developed gluteal muscles and skin folds; normal male genitalia with no visible fistula; clear urine without meconium contamination

node-4.label: Catheter could not be inserted more than half an inch into the anal opening

node-5.label: Abdominal X-ray showed multiple dilated bowel loops, including an S-shaped dilated bowel loop extending downward toward the pelvis, indicative of the sigmoid colon; echocardiogram, renal ultrasound, and vertebral X-ray were normal with no indications of VACTERL association

attrs.why: Radiologist analysis supports anorectal malformation as the best fit, reinforcing the existing evidence of catheter resistance at half an inch, normal anus position, dilated loops with S-shaped pelvic sigmoid, and lower GI contrast showing no rectal passage beyond the anal canal. Confidence is raised from 0.88 to 0.90.

Radiologist explicitly favors low-type anorectal malformation over Hirschsprung disease. The anorectal-level obstruction without a transition zone on lower GI contrast makes Hirschsprung less likely. Confidence is lowered from 0.20 to 0.15.

The new lower gastrointestinal contrast finding of no passage of rectal contrast is inconsistent with meconium ileus/atresia, in which contrast would typically outline a microcolon and dilated proximal bowel rather than being blocked at the anorectal level. Combined with the catheter obstruction located at the anus rather than at an ileal level, confidence decreases from 0.15 to 0.12.
Radiologist states VACTERL is refuted. Normal echocardiogram, renal ultrasound, and vertebral X-ray already argue against it. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.03.

node-12.label: Low-type anorectal malformation with partial anal canal patency (e.g., anal stenosis or membranous atresia)
